canregtools

Overview

Canregtools is an R package designed to streamline the analysis workflow for Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) data. It aims to improve the efficiency, accuracy, and reproducibility of cancer registry data processing, thereby supporting standardized, and routine PBCR analytical workflows.

Install

Currently, the package is not available on CRAN, but you can install the development version of canregtools from https://gigu003.r-universe.dev/.

install.packages('canregtools', repos = c('https://gigu003.r-universe.dev', 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))

View the vignette

After installing canregtools, list the available vignettes or open the main user guide directly:

browseVignettes("canregtools")
vignette("using-canregtools", package = "canregtools")

The vignette explains the canreg and fbswicd objects, data-management functions such as cr_select() and cr_filter(), and the workflow for calculating rates and quality indicators. It is also available in the package website at articles/using-canregtools.html.

Usage 

library(canregtools)
data("canregs")
registry <- canregs[[1]]
summary_object <- count_canreg(registry, cancer_type = "big")

asr <- create_asr(summary_object, year, sex, cancer)
quality <- create_quality(summary_object, cancer)
age_rate <- create_age_rate(summary_object)

Registry dictionaries can be isolated by project. User overrides are combined with built-in defaults and take effect immediately:

options(canregtools.dict_dir = file.path("config", "canregtools"))
mapping <- data.frame(
  regicode = c("410103", "410307"),
  area_type = c("910000", "920000"),
  hdi = c("high", "low")
)
cr_map(mapping, attr = c("area_type", "hdi"))
ls_dict("hdi")

Use write_regicode() for multilingual registry labels and reset_dict() to clear overrides with a backup. Legacy files are backed up on their next update; see the vignette for migration details.

The main workflow is:

Excel/data frames -> canreg(s) -> fbswicd(s)
                  -> rates, quality indicators, and reports

For detailed input requirements, data-management functions, validation, and reproducible analysis options, see the using-canregtools vignette.
